title: Chromatic Alchemy Post-Process Lab
description: A dragon perches on the rim of a translucent teacup in a moody scene. The user manipulates a chain of post-processing effects—bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, tone-mapping, and color grading—where each effect's energy is drawn from a shared 'mana pool' (conservation law). Adjusting one effect's intensity automatically reduces the budget available to others, and undo/redo lets the user step through their history of adjustments.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) with EffectComposer from three/addons. Load DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb centered at origin and DragonDispersion.glb scaled and positioned so the dragon sits on the teacup's rim, facing outward. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,3) looking at (0,0.5,0). Add an HDR-style lighting rig: one warm DirectionalLight, one cool RimLight, and a soft AmbientLight. Enable OrbitControls. Build a post-processing chain with five ShaderPass effects: (1) Bloom (UnrealBloomPass), (2) Chromatic Aberration (custom uniform float strength), (3) Vignette (custom uniform float darkness and offset), (4) Tone-Mapping exposure (custom uniform float exposure), (5) Color-Grading hue-shift (custom uniform float hueShift). Implement a conservation-law mana pool of 100 units. Each effect's intensity maps to mana cost: bloom 0-30, chromatic aberration 0-20, vignette 0-20, tone-mapping 0-15, hue-shift 0-15. Display an HTML overlay panel on the left with five labeled sliders, a mana bar showing remaining budget, and Undo/Redo buttons. When a slider moves, compute its new mana cost; if total exceeds 100, clamp the slider and flash the mana bar red. Each slider change pushes a snapshot (all five values) onto an undo stack (max 30). Redo stack clears on new input. Undo restores the previous snapshot and updates all sliders and uniforms. Redo re-applies. Show the current step number (e.g., 'Step 7/12'). The interaction requires 10-14 steps: user must explore combinations, hit the mana cap, redistribute, undo mistakes, and redo. Render at window resolution with antialiasing. The dragon's dispersion material and teacup's transmission should visually react to the post-process chain, making the creative exploration rewarding.
